question.problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T([\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}])=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2u+v) \\ uv\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2u+v)$ and $y=uv.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =\frac{2}{2u+v} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =\frac{1}{2u+v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =v & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{2u+v} & \frac{1}{2u+v} \\ \,\text{ }v\, & \,\text{ }u\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{2}{2u+v}\cdot u-\frac{1}{2u+v}\cdot v \\  & =\frac{2u-v}{2u+v}.\end{aligned}
$$
